text:
lina (ML Eng): heads-up — bringing up nova-alpha-11b into the GTN pilot. ran a micro-slice we nicknamed 'samplehouse' (~2.5k convo turns). ran int6 and int8 quant variants. need a short cost-vs-quality routing recommendation and a fallback/playbook. baseline in prod is orion-7b-int4.

yusuf (ML Eng): can you drop the short summary numbers here? quick snapshot is fine.

lina (ML Eng): sure — pasted quick summary from the smoke run:

```
summary:
model                | quant | p95 latency | tokens/sec | max_throughput | avg_accept_score | cost_per_1M_tokens
nova-alpha-11b       | int8  | 480ms       | 120        | 400 rps        | 87.3             | $1.20
nova-alpha-11b       | int6  | 510ms       | 140        | 460 rps        | 86.9             | $0.95
orion-7b             | int4  | 220ms       | 300        | 1000 rps       | 83.4             | $0.60
``` 

notes: accept_score = internal GTN composite (0-100) combining relevance, factuality, and style; sample size ~2.5k turns, mixed short/long queries (median 180 tokens). p95 measured on host pool without dedicated reserved capacity.

olga (Data Sci): quality delta between int8 and int6 is small (~0.4 points), not significant on many slices. however on longform summarization (>800 tokens) int8 preserves structure better and has fewer hallucination markers in manual review.

marc (Infra): infra notes — int6 currently uses the new kernel path that lets us pack higher batch sizes; memory footprint is slightly lower so you get higher throughput for same GPU. int8 still edges on some long-context kernels due to fp fallback. also: p95 will improve if we move to dedicated pools (we're seeing noisy colocated hosts).

sophia (Product): product constraints: latency tail and hallucination risk matter. tradeoffs ok if we can guarantee failover. thinking: hybrid routing by token length might cover our GTN SLAs and keep costs sensible.

yusuf (ML Eng): proposed routing policy (quick):
- requests <= 128 tokens -> orion-7b-int4 (cheap short-turn model)
- requests 129-512 tokens -> nova-alpha-11b-int6 (sweet spot: throughput + ~same quality)
- requests >512 tokens -> nova-alpha-11b-int8 (preserve structure on longform)
- fallback: if int6 p95 > 750ms or error_rate > 0.5% -> route to int8 or to orion-7b-int4 depending on SLA criticality

lina (ML Eng): rollout plan: 5% canary for 48h, monitor metrics: accept_score delta, hallucination_rate (manual / automated), latency p95/p99, error_rate, cost/tokens. flag name: nova-alpha/gtp-hybrid-v1. if accept_score delta > 1.5 points or hallucination_rate doubles, rollback immediately.

dev-bot: deploy job created: https://deploys.redwood.ai/ops/12345 (canary 5% -> nova-alpha/gtp-hybrid-v1). :shipit:

marc (Infra): FYI opened infra ticket INF-8342 for tuning int6 kernel packing and a dedicated canary pool. also we should schedule a small dedicated run for 12h to get stable p99 data.

olga (Data Sci): I'll add three evaluation slices to the GTN dashboard: code-completion, legal-QA, multi-turn summarization. ran quick sample vs prod orion-7b and added prompt set under /evals/samplehouse.

lina (ML Eng): ack. scheduling canary tonight 10pm PST. tagging @sophia for final GTN signoff before we flip >5%.

sophia (Product): sounds good — will review the evaluation slices and give green by EOD. quick ask: include a short user-facing degradation note we can show if we have to rollback (one-liner).

marc (Infra): note for ops runbook: prefer graceful fallback to orion-7b-int4 for very short queries to reduce cost spikes; for long requests prefer int8 to avoid content regressions. added runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/nova-alpha-routing

lina (ML Eng): great — thanks all. will post canary results in this thread after 24h and again after 48h. :eyes:
